Job Title: Carpenter
Company: Fineform Concrete Pty Ltd
Location: Welshpool, WA 6106
Salary: $90,000 to $100,000 + superannuation
Employment Type: Full-Time

About Us
Fineform Concrete Pty Ltd is a leading contractor in formwork and concrete construction across Western Australia. Based in Welshpool, we specialise in high-quality commercial and civil projects. Our team is known for precision, safety, and professionalism.
As we expand our operations, we are seeking a qualified and experienced Carpenter to join our full-time workforce.

Key Duties & Responsibilities:

•	Interpret technical drawings and formwork designs to accurately determine materials, measurements, and construction requirements for civil and structural concrete works.
•	Select, measure, and cut timber and other formwork materials to specifications required for complex industrial, commercial, and high-rise projects.
•	Construct and install custom formwork systems for concrete foundations, walls, columns, slabs, and suspended structures.
•	Assemble and erect framework and falsework, ensuring structural integrity and precise alignment in accordance with project tolerances.
•	Collaborate with site supervisors and concreting teams to ensure formwork is completed and ready for timely concrete placement.
•	Install reinforcements and embedded fixtures into formwork as per engineering specifications and site requirements.
•	Dismantle and strip formwork post-pour while preserving reusable materials and maintaining site safety standards.
•	Carry out formwork repairs, adjustments, and modifications to accommodate design changes or project-specific needs.
•	Operate and maintain carpentry tools, equipment, and machinery to ensure quality workmanship and efficiency
•	Adhere to FineForm’s safety protocols and contribute to maintaining a clean, organised, and hazard-free work environment on remote, metro, and offshore sites.

Requirements:

•	Relevant qualification
•	Minimum 2-3years' carpentry experience 
•	Ability to read and interpret technical drawings and plans
•	Strong focus on safety, quality, and teamwork


Should you be interested, send us your application ASAP!

result.description:
About the role:   
We are looking for a passionate physiotherapist to work with a paediatric caseload, working within NDIS model of funding. All applicants will be considered but paediatric experience or interest is desirable. 
You will be surrounded by a supportive group of physiotherapists, including mentoring from our senior clinician physiotherapist with over 20 years’ experience in paediatrics. 
 
We are looking for an evidence-minded professional who is eager to self-reflect, adapt and grow with the most recent recommendations in paediatric physiotherapy. This includes working within models such as keyworker, routines-based and family-centred care. 
 
We work both in the community and in our up-to-date clinic spaces. Includes opportunity to provide pilates-based intervention using our paediatric and adult reformers and utilise our modern gym facilities. Opportunities to expand and develop our current offerings - we are a regional partner of Freedom Wheels and provide specialised bike trials for clients in the Ballarat region. 
 
A unique opportunity to work collaboratively in a multidisciplinary team of speech pathologists, occupational therapists and educational advisors, to achieve the best outcomes for children and families. We are motivated by getting to work with clients long-term and see real change and outcomes on their journey. 
 
 Key Duties and Responsibilities:  

 
	 This role will be responsible for day-to-day clinical services within the Therapy, Education, and Support Services team. 
	 Clinical service delivery under the National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS) 
	 Engage in and lead clinical work that is guided by evidence-based neuro-affirming practice 
	 Develop and communicate ideas for innovation and improvement 
	 Recognise and support cultural, spiritual and neurodiversity of customers 
	 Ensure clear customer documentation 
	 Work collaboratively, with enthusiasm, recognising contributions from all members of the team 
	 Actively participate in the staff supervision process 
	 For those with experience, an opportunity to support other staff 
	 Participate in student placements 
	 Be solution-focused, honest and responsive to new directions and program requirements 
 

 Qualifications and experience: 

 
	 Bachelor degree or equivalent 
	 Current registration with Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (AHPRA) 
	 Safety Screening, including WWCC, NDIS Worker Screening Check 
 

 If you would like to learn more about this role, we would love to hear from you!   Apply Now

Employment Type: Full-Time
Salary: $79,500 per annum, plus superannuation

Panel Beater - Full-Time Position

At A1 Auto & Bodywork, based in Sumner, QLD, we are hiring for various positions and are currently seeking an experienced Panel Beater to join our busy workshop. You will be responsible for restoring damaged vehicle bodies to their original condition, from dent and scratch repairs through to collision restoration and full panel replacement. Reporting to the owner, you will be responsible for ensuring jobs are completed efficiently, safely and to a high standard. This position offers an excellent opportunity to join a growing, well-established business with a strong reputation for quality workmanship and customer service.

Qualifications & Experience:
More than 2 years of experience as a Panel Beater
A minimum of Certificate III in Automotive Body Repair Technology would be highly regarded
Sound knowledge of vehicle body structures, panel alignment and welding techniques
Strong attention to detail and problem-solving skills
Good customer communication skills
Reliable and punctual

Your key responsibilities will include:
Examining damaged vehicle bodies and estimating time, cost and materials required for repair
Removing badly damaged sections using flame-cutting and welding equipment, and welding in replacement sections
Removing damaged panels and parts, and installing and aligning replacement parts
Hammering out dents, buckles and other defects using hand tools, machine presses and jacks
Filling small dents and creases that cannot be worked out, and preparing surfaces for painting
Aligning wheels, and repairing or replacing steering and suspension components affected by collision damage
Fitting and aligning glass windows, windscreens, and window mechanisms
Measuring vehicles using computerised equipment to determine and correct misalignment
Liaising with customers and insurers regarding the scope and progress of repair work


If this sounds like the right fit, we would love to hear from you - please submit your resume, along with a brief cover letter telling us why you are the perfect fit for the role, by clicking on the Apply Now button.

Adarsh Australia is a leading manufacturer of custom metal and plastic components in Perth, Western Australia.

With over 30 years of experience, dependable customer service and quality products, Adarsh Australia is the preferred manufacturer for Perth and multinational companies.

We are currently seeking a qualified CNC machinist (Metal Machinist – First Class) for a full-time role as a result of our continued growth. The role primarily involves programming, setting and operating Okuma CNC machines.

Skills & Experience:

- Trade qualified machinist to the level of at least a Certificate III.
- Minimum of 3 years’ experience in a manufacturing environment (post apprenticeship).
- CNC machining experience, Okuma preferred (setting, operating and programming)
- Keen eye for detail and commitment to quality.
- Able to work unsupervised but also be a team player.
- Technical knowledge as a CNC machinist with an understanding of and experience of SolidWorks/SolidCAM.
- Clear understanding of geometric dimensioning and tolerancing principles.
- Excellent verbal and written communication skill
- Reliable, hardworking with a positive attitude.

Key Responsibilities:

- Working with multiple CNC machines (milling centres and/or lathes) to successfully produce the desired metal or plastic product.
- Interfacing with various team members to achieve the desired outcomes as outlined by senior management.
- Setting up and operating multiple CNC machines.
- Selection of best tool and manufacturing method for application.
- Verifying components to the manufacturing specifications and tolerances (QC).
- Reading and understanding technical/manufacturing/engineering drawings & specifications.
- Understanding geometric dimensioning and tolerancing principles.
- Reliable and secure, full-time position with a long-established local manufacturing company.

Expected annual pay will be from $80,000 to $90,000 per year on a standard work week. Overtime hours are available.

The role is based in Malaga, Western Australia.

To apply please send your resume and cover letter to hr@adarsh.com.au or click the ‘Apply’ button.
